response.sql: WITH d AS (SELECT m.department AS department, COUNT(DISTINCT i.link_to_member) AS cnt FROM income i JOIN member mem ON mem.member_id = i.link_to_member JOIN major m ON m.major_id = mem.link_to_major GROUP BY m.department), s AS (SELECT department, cnt, CAST(cnt AS REAL) / (SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM d) AS share FROM d), a AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT SUM(s.cnt) AS total_count, AVG(s.share) AS avg_share, AVG(s.share - a.avg_share) AS avg_share_diff FROM s CROSS JOIN a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share

assumptions.assumption: Departments are grouped by the major.department value as-is; the same department name in different colleges is treated as one department. Departments with NULL department would form one group.
The average of shares in output (2) and (3) is computed over the retained departments only (those above the all-department average), while the threshold average is over all departments.

alternatives.interpretation: Outputs (2) and (3) use the all-department average share for (2) rather than the average over retained departments; (3) is still the average over retained departments of share minus the all-department average.
